b_h2_cases: Types of cases our {City} car accident attorneys represent
b_cases_intro: Every crash is different. What they have in common is an adjuster deciding what your injury is worth before you have said a word. These are the {City} cases we handle most.
b_case_1_b: The other driver says the light was yellow. The intersection camera says otherwise — for about a week, until it is overwritten. We send preservation letters the day you call, then pull the signal timing and any business camera pointed at that corner.
b_case_2_b: A DUI arrest is not the same as your civil claim, and the criminal case will not pay your bills. We run both tracks: the police investigation and, where the facts support it, a claim against the bar or restaurant that overserved the driver under California's dram shop rules.
b_case_3_b: The most common crash and the most underpaid. Insurers concede fault, then argue the impact was too minor to hurt anyone. Photographs of a bumper are not a medical opinion, and we make them prove that with a doctor instead of a claims note.
b_case_4_b: Uber and Lyft carry up to $1,000,000 in coverage, but only when the app was in the right state at the moment of impact. Whether you were the passenger, the driver, or in the other car, the first job is proving which policy was live — and that record sits with the company, not with you.
b_case_5_b: Three, four, five cars on the 405 or the 710, and every insurer blaming the car behind. These cases are won by identifying every policy and reconstructing the order of impacts early, before each carrier settles into its story.
b_h2_24h: Car accident attorneys in {City}, CA open 24 hours
b_24h_p1: Crashes do not keep office hours. Neither do we. You can reach a real person about your {City} crash at any hour, any day — nights, weekends and holidays included. Not a recording that promises a callback, and not a chatbot. A person who takes down what happened and gets a lawyer moving on it.
b_24h_p2: That matters more than it sounds. The evidence that decides these cases — intersection video, store cameras, a witness who still remembers the light — has a shelf life measured in days. The insurance company's adjuster is often assigned within hours of the crash. Calling at 11pm on a Saturday instead of Monday morning can be the difference between having that footage and arguing without it.
b_h2_why: Why turn to a car accident attorney in {City} after a crash
b_why_intro: Insurance companies profit when you take less. You are not obligated to hire anyone, and plenty of small claims resolve fine without a lawyer. Here is what changes when you do have one.
b_why_1_b: No retainer, no hourly bill, nothing out of your pocket. We front every case cost — filing fees, medical records, accident reconstruction, expert witnesses — and we are paid a percentage only if we recover money for you. If we do not win, you do not owe us a fee.
b_why_2_b: More than {totalRecovered} recovered for injured people across five decades of California practice. In one recent case the insurance company's first and best offer was $85,000. After Kyle Hindin litigated it, the case resolved for $375,000. Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome.
b_why_3_t: We fight to get you paid while you recover
b_why_3_b: Medical bills do not wait for a settlement. We help you get treatment on a lien so you can see a doctor without paying up front, deal with the hospital and the health plan on billing, and keep the adjuster's calls away from you entirely. Your job is the physical therapy. Ours is everything else.
b_why_4_t: Award winning accident attorneys serving {City} and all of Los Angeles County
b_why_4_b: Kyle Hindin has been named a Super Lawyers Rising Star every year from 2022 through 2026 and is a member of the Consumer Attorneys Association of Los Angeles. Robert Hindin founded the firm and has been licensed in California since 1975. We work out of one real office in West Los Angeles — 11400 W Olympic Blvd, Suite 200 — and take cases across {City} and the whole of Los Angeles County.
b_why_5_b: The consultation costs nothing and obligates you to nothing. Tell us what happened and we will tell you straight whether you have a case, what it is likely worth, and what the deadlines are. If you do not need a lawyer, we will say so.
b_deadlines_h: The deadlines that decide your case
b_deadlines_p1: In California you generally have two years from the date of the crash to file suit. If a city bus, a county vehicle or any government agency is involved, you may have as little as six months to file a government claim — miss that and the case can end before it starts.
b_deadlines_p2: The practical clock is much faster. Camera footage is overwritten in days. Witnesses stop returning calls. The other driver's story firms up after they speak to their own insurer. And if you wait to see a doctor, the gap between the crash and your first visit becomes the adjuster's main argument that you were not really hurt.
